Sports.title: Man Utd identify £62.5m star as ultimate successor to Bruno Fernandes after Michael Carrick tactical masterclass
Sports.content:
MATHEUS CUNHA and Bruno Fernandes won the head tennis tournament during Manchester United’s training camp in Ireland and combined again at Chelsea last week.

Fernandes has assisted the Brazilian’s last two goals — both of them winners — and the Red Devils have a new clutch player.





The first time they came up against each other was in a pre-season friendly between United and Atletico Madrid, in Oslo in 2022.

Cunha got the better of the Portuguese so strikingly that day that the United talisman cynically fouled him.

It happened again at Molineux on Boxing Day in 2024, when Fernandes was sent off in the 47th minute for two bookable offences.

Cunha scored the first and created the second in Wolves’ 2-0 win.



The 26-year-old is the probable heir to Fernandes, 31, whenever he leaves Old Trafford.

United’s skipper has a contract until 2028, by which time Cunha will have been there for three years.

Succession planning has not been the club’s forte.

Down the Mancunian Way, Manchester City replaced one Silva with another and Bernardo has been gold, just as David was. Kevin De Bruyne made way for Rayan Cherki, a maverick who is developing into another classy playmaker under Pep Guardiola.



United’s move for Cunha last year was partially to offset the possibility of Fernandes accepting Saudi dosh from Al-Nassr.

Instead, the pair have formed a clinical combination and interim coach Michael Carrick has easily accommodated both No 10s without considering a switch back to Ruben Amorim’s 3-4-3 system.

Cunha occasionally played on the left for his previous clubs and was the obvious option there to offset the loss of Patrick Dorgu in January.

Dorgu has missed more than the 12 weeks his hamstring injury was expected to sideline him for but his absence has not been a major problem.



Since he regained his place in the side, Cunha has three key goals and won two penalties.

The spot-kick he earned against Crystal Palace on March 1 was a game-changer as United were 1-0 down and went on to win 2-1.

At Bournemouth later that month, Cunha gave Alex Jimenez the runaround and the Spaniard’s shirt tug enabled Fernandes to convert again from 12 yards.

Cunha was of interest to Arsenal while at Wolves last season and it is impossible to envisage his flair in Mikel Arteta’s agricultural side now.



Eberechi Eze, a similar playmaker, was fleetingly considered by United and seems to have had all the joy coached out of him by Arteta since his summer switch from Palace.

Amorim was so wedded to the doomed 3-4-3 that constrained United that it is curious he made a beeline for a free spirit like Cunha.

Their working relationship was brief — just three months — but the £62.5million summer signing was effective under the Portuguese coach, even when United’s form was patchy.

Harry Maguire was the hero in the Red Devils’ first victory at Anfield in nearly ten years in October.

But Cunha’s game management was masterful, particularly as he had only just returned from international duty in South Korea and Japan.



He was frustrated by his early goal drought and did not get off the mark until his ninth United appearance, against Brighton, but now has eight in 24 games.

That is a respectable return from a forward whose 15 strikes almost singlehandedly maintained Wolves’ Premier League status last season.

Some at Molineux felt Cunha and United would be a mismatch, with Old Trafford staff warned he could be difficult to deal with.

Their experiences have been the complete opposite and Cunha has been charm personified during his handful of dealings with the media.



United sources believe he has a sense of belonging now he has the opportunity to represent such an historic club.

Cunha was a dream to speak to when SunSport conducted an exclusive interview with him at Carrington in November.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Afterwards, I told him was a better talker than Fernandes. He was grateful for that compliment.

It would be some going if he turns out to be a better United player than Fernandes.

Sports.title: ‘Disgraceful’ – Man Utd fans furious after Dominic Calvert-Lewin escapes red card for ‘hair pull’ on Marc Cucurella
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans are livid that Dominic Calvert-Lewin has escaped a red card for hair pulling just weeks after a Red Devil got his marching orders for doing it to him.

The Leeds striker appears to get a good handful of Marc Cucurella‘s nest during the FA Cup semi-final against Chelsea, but no action was taken.





Fans were livid at the apparent double standards and took to X to complain.

One user said: “Gave Martinez red for less.”

Another posted: “The rules are obviously not consistent in application and that’s bad for the league.”

A third commented: “Everyone already knew there’s a bias against United. And now only a couple of weeks and multiple hair pulls later, it’s not even debatable anymore. But it’s pointless complaining. Teams have to begin legal proceedings against PGMOL.”



It was only a few days ago that an FA panel denied Man United’s appeal against Lisandro Martinez’s sending off for a hair pull – ironically against Calvert Lewin.

Earlier in the season, Everton’s Michael Keane was also sent off for a hair pull on Wolves’ Tolu Arokodare.

The panel has said hair pulling “ought not to be tolerated” in its reasons for upholding a three-game ban for Martinez earlier this month.

In a written report, the commission said it accepted other forms of violent conduct “carry a much higher risk of harm to an opponent”.



But: “In the wider interests of football ‘hair pulling’ ought not to be tolerated and should be discouraged through consistent punishment.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Consistently enforcing the rules is half the issue.

Man United boss Michael Carrick thought the decision was ‘shocking’ and encouraged the FA to know the difference between touching and aggressively touching.

“It is not aggressive, there is no jolt, no tug. We have got to be careful where the game is going. It is a shocking decision, absolutely shocking. The red card, that is really concerning. I know he touched his hair. There is a difference to really aggressively touching it.”

Chelsea are currently leading the semi-final at Wembley 1-0, but if Calvert-Lewin plays a role in getting the Yorkshire side getting back into the game the Blues may well share the anger of the United fans.

Sports.title: Newcastle ‘chasing shock transfer for Chelsea outcast Nicolas Jackson’ after Bayern refused to trigger permanent deal
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE are interested in signing Chelsea ace Nicolas Jackson after Bayern Munich decided to end his loan this summer.

Jackson, 24, joined Bayern last year for the season after falling down the pecking order at Stamford Bridge and has since amassed 10 goals and four assists in 29 appearances across all competitions.





The treble chasers agreed a loan deal for the striker that included an obligation to buy for £56.2million if certain conditions were met.

That clause would have been triggered if the Senegal international had played at least 45 minutes out of 40 matches.

But that didn’t happen as Jackson has played second fiddle to star striker Harry Kane, who has registered a staggering total of 53 goals and six assists in 45 appearances this term.

And thus Bayern director of sport Max Eberl confirmed Jackson will return to Chelsea in June.



Eberl told ZDF: “We will not trigger the option for Nicolas Jackson.”

According to talkSPORT, that latest development led to interest from Newcastle ahead of the summer transfer window.

The Magpies will be looking for quality reinforcement at centre-forward after Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa both failed to impress after Alexander Isak’s record £130million move to Liverpool last summer.

Chelsea will look to sell Jackson as he would command a high fee the West Londoners would especially need if they miss out on Champions League qualification with them currently eighth in the Premier League.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The relationship between the Senegalese star and the Blues is said to be damaged as the club almost scrapped his loan switch to Bayern at the 11th hour last year.

That was because last summer’s transfer signing Liam Delap got injured and Chelsea thought they would need Jackson for depth at No9.

But the ex-Villarreal star was ultimately allowed to move to Munich after the club cancelled Marc Guiu’s loan at Sunderland.

Sports.title: Emotional Frank Lampard’s celebrates Coventry’s Premier League return in front of packed crowd including wife Christine
Sports.content:
FRANK LAMPARD and his Coventry troops are celebrating their return to the Premier League in front of their own fans at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Sky Blues defeated Wrexham 3-1 in their final home league game to ensure the Welsh side will partake in a three-way battle for the final playoff spot alongside Hull City and Derby County next weekend.





Wrexham’s Hollywood owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, jokingly tried to tease Coventry into a midweek trip to Las Vegas in a bid to boost their chances.

Sadly for them, the champions remained on their game and put on a show in their final home game of the campaign.

They will close their campaign away at Watford next weekend.

Lampard, 47, has proven his worth at Coventry after a stop-start management career and clearly savoured the victorious scenes on Sunday afternoon.



His wife Christine and two of his four children joined him on the pitch for the celebrations before he gave a speech to the jubilant fans.

In his speech after the trophy lift, Lampard dedicated the triumph to his wife.

“The biggest thank you – a football club is only as big as the people who support it.

“You’ve supported it. You’ve been down a lot. You’ve been to different stadiums with this team, other teams – all the teams. Because when you’re born this way you’re never going to change right?

“I have to say, one of the biggest pleasures we get as a group is giving you the joy of this moment. So this moment is yours.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Chelsea legend has won 44 of his 81 games in charge of Coventry since arriving in November 2024.

His work in the midlands has been so impressive that some reports have linked him to a third spell in the dugout at Stamford Bridge.

But Coventry chairman Doug King believes Lampard is happy just where he is.

“You can see how emotionally connected [Lampard] is with the city, you can see what it meant to him to get promotion and then the title and I think he’s found a happy place at the moment.”

“It doesn’t mean there’s not going to be some staggering bid for him in the summer and he’ll have to make his choices, because he’s shown his credentials as a high-quality head coach, but I’m not going to comment on that, I can’t control it.”

Sports.title: Football Wag Apollonia Llewellyn almost erupts out of skintight top as fans call her ‘dangerously attractive’
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL Wag Apollonia Llewellyn took social media by storm during a trip to Spain.

Apollonia, 26, jetted off to Mallorca and took a few raunchy snaps while enjoying the sun.





The former boxing ring girl then immediately shared the pics on her Instagram.

Apollonia posted the following caption: “Hello Spain.”

Sports.title: ‘We’ve heard this before…’ – Arsenal fans fearing worst after Mikel Arteta offers Kai Havertz injury update
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans are worried Kai Havertz will miss the title run-in – despite chief Mikel Arteta revealing the German’s injury did not appear to be serious.

An early stunner from Eberechi Eze allowed the Gunners to seal a 1-0 win over Newcastle and retake top spot in the Premier League.





But Havertz, 26, cut a forlorn figure when he was forced off in the first half and headed straight down the tunnel.

It is yet another blow for the striker, who was ruled out for more than FOUR MONTHS when he picked up an injury in the win over Manchester United on the opening weekend of the season.

Arteta attempted to alleviate concerns of another lengthy spell out of action during his post-match media conference.



The Gunners boss said: “I don’t know how serious it is. It didn’t look too big.

“The action, the way he describes it, is not too sharp. But we have to wait and see.”

But Arsenal fans raced on to social media to make it clear they are still fearing the worst as they look to be crowned champions for the first time in 22 years.

One said: “Arteta: ‘Should not be too bad’. We’ve heard this before. Last time it was ‘minor’ and he was out for six weeks. Just say he’s fine Mikel. Just say it.”



Another added: “Not too sharp in Arteta speak is either a two-day rest or a three-month disappearance. I’m currently holding my breath until I see him in the training photos.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A third chimed in: “Doesn’t have to look too bad for Havertz to spend three months in the hospital, we know him.”

A fourth noted: “Havertz injuries don’t always look that bad but the outcome will be.”



A fifth commented: “We’ve been lied to before bro.”

Injuries have limited Havertz to just 20 appearances in all competitions this season – with him notching five goals along the way.

The former Chelsea man, who won the Champions League at Stamford Bridge, is facing a race against time to prove his fitness ahead of Arsenal’s trip to Atletico Madrid on Wednesday.

Sports.title: Vegan club Forest Green Rovers answer claim fan was removed for eating bacon sandwich
Sports.content:
Vegan club Forest Green Rovers answer claim fan was removed for eating bacon sandwich

A viral video has claimed that football supporter was removed over a bacon sandwich on Saturday, but Forest Green Rovers have moved to refute the suggestion

View 2 Images Forest Green Rovers have dismissed social media reports that a fan was removed from their ground for having a bacon sandwich. (Image: PA)

National League side Forest Green Rovers have broken their silence, dismissing social media reports that a fan was removed from their ground for having a bacon sandwich. Footage emerged on online platforms showing a fan being ejected from The New Lawn Stadium during their clash with Morecambe, with the suggestion that he had brought in his own food.

‌



Forest Green, who were members of the Football League for seven years before their relegation to the non-league system in 2024, became the world's first vegan football club in 2015. The decision was made by chairman and environmentalist Dale Vince as they scrapped meat and fish for plant-based foods.

‌



Therefore taking in a bacon sandwich would have been viewed against the club's move to switch meat for a plant-based menu. However, the Green Devils have issued a statement rejecting the claim as they suggested that the individual was removed for failing to adhere to repeated warnings from stewards after repeated warnings for displaying some "over-exuberance".

‌



Man Utd identify another Casemiro replacement as summer transfer plans step up READ MORE :

In a post to X, they wrote: "We are aware of a video circulating online following our game against Morecambe yesterday.

"Contrary to social media opinion & wisdom, the ejection was nothing to do with bacon sarnies (sic) more a little 'over exuberance' on the last day of the season. After repeated warnings, the stewards were left with no choice and the gentleman was ejected from the stadium. #neverletthetruthgetinthewayofagoodstory #slownewsday."

The video seemingly emerged on TikTok, where the caption, displayed for around 18 seconds, read: "Solicitor/Morecambe fan removed for sneaking Bacon butty into Forest Green Rovers."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The footage shows three stewards removing the gentleman before X users reposted the video onto a different platform. How much football the supposed Morecambe missed is unknown but his side ended their incident-hit campaign with a 5-0 defeat to Robbie Savage's side.

It means that The Shrimps have been relegated in three of their last four seasons and have fallen from League One to playing National League North, regional football, next season.

‌



For Forest Green, they ended Savage's first season in charge on a high after adding gloss on their playoff-clinching campaign. They face a trip to Boreham Wood on Wednesday in the National League playoff eliminator for a place in the semi-final, where they will travel to Carlisle United.

View 2 Images Robbie Savage has guided Forest Green to the National League playoffs in his first season. (Image: Getty Images)

In an interview from 2015, Vince explained the decision to switch to an entire plant-based menu. He said: "As a football club, we stopped serving meat to our players, fans and staff about four seasons ago.

‌



"We've been on a mission since then to introduce our fans to this new world. When you drop the meat and two veg approach, a whole new world of food options opens up.

"The gap between vegetarian and vegan food is actually quite small; it's a step rather than a leap to take. A lot of our food has been vegan for some time now, and this season we've taken the last small step."

In a blog post to his website dalevince.com, the Forest Green owner claimed that the change has been profitable, even beating meat-based catering across the country to win Menu of the Year from Sport and Leisure Catering Magazine.

Sports.title: Police 'aware' of video appearing to show York City player punching fan
Sports.content:
Police 'aware' of video appearing to show York City player punching fan

York City were dramatically promoted to the Football League on Saturday with a dramatic victory against Rochdale but the post-match celebrations were marred by a few unsavoury scenes

View 3 Images Police say they are aware of the alleged incident (Image: Getty Images)

Police say they are ‘aware’ of a video appearing to show a York City player punching a fan following their dramatic promotion. York secured a place in League Two on Saturday with a thrilling draw against promotion rivals Rochdale.

‌



Rochdale thought they had secured victory, with Emmanuel Dieseruvwe scoring in the fifth minute of stoppage time. That triggered a mass pitch invasion, with fans flooding the pitch.

‌



But the game continued, with York eventually scoring an equaliser in the 103rd minute of the game through Josh Stones to snatch the only automatic promotion spot. It saw York finish top of the table on 108 points, while Rochdale were second in 106.

‌



However, the dramatic scenes saw an incident involving a fan putting his hands on a player, who was on his knees with his head against the ground. Two stewards eventually got involved but the player managed to break free and appeared to strike the supporter in the face.

Rochdale vs York ends in dramatic scenes after pitch invasions and controversial goal READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

A video has since gone viral on social media, with Greater Manchester Police having issued a statement. It read: "We are aware of a video that is circulating of a possible assault involving a player and we have linked in with both clubs and the National League. We will be further assessing the video and reviewing CCTV of the incident."

‌



It took six minutes for the home side to clear the pitch of supporters before the game got back underway. And York boss Stuart Maynard that time actually helped his side regroup and eventually get their equaliser.

“I think that helped,” said Maynard. “That time to reflect.

View 3 Images Fans invaded the pitch after both goals at Spotland (Image: Chris Nutton/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock)

‌



"It’s twice in two weeks, we’ve had our heart broken that we’ve had one hand firmly gripped on the trophy and it got taken away for all of 60 seconds.

“But look, they’re a group of winners in there. They’re warriors. They keep going all the way to the end.

"I’m so proud of them all. I told them we’ve just got to get the ball forward. They came over and we just said, everyone go up front, bar the goalkeeper.

‌



View 3 Images York City sealed promotiom with their dramatic draw against Rochdale (Image: Getty Images)

"We’ve got to get it forward. And Callum Howe said it, there’s going to be one big moment - and there was.”

Rochdale, who have offered their support to a three-up campaign in the National League, will now head into the playoffs for a place in League Two. They have earned an automatic spot in the semi-finals and will take on either Scunthorpe United or Southend United, who clash in an eliminator on Tuesday evening.

Sports.title: Laura Woods struck by football live on TNT before FA Cup semi-final pundits get soaked
Sports.content:
Laura Woods struck by football live on TNT before FA Cup semi-final pundits get soaked

TNT Sports' pre-match coverage of the FA Cup semi-final between Chelsea and Leeds United descended into chaos after sprinklers and stray footballs intervened.

View 2 Images Pre-match coverage of the FA Cup semi-final between Leeds and Chelsea. (Image: TNT Sports)

Former Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole was left red-faced when a stray touch sent a rogue ball at TNT Sports presenter Laura Woods. The coverage of the FA Cup semi-final between the Blues and Premier League rivals, Leeds United, descended into chaos with the Wembley sprinklers further disrupting the build-up.

‌



The coverage was stationed pitchside, towards the Leeds warm-up, when the incident occurred after a deflected rondo pass squirted towards the TNT Sports analysts. Cole turned around and dangled a left leg towards the stray pass, miscontrolling it before it brushed the hand of a shocked Woods.

‌



Their coverage was then impacted when the Wembley sprinkler routine diverted towards them. The panel, which also included former Leeds striker Jermaine Beckford, tried to continue with business as usual.

‌



Police 'aware' of video appearing to show York City player punching fan READ MORE :

However, they couldn't resist bringing up the gaffe. Woods, who stood left of the picture presenting, said: "OK, the Leeds players have headed back in, a minute ago they were so close to us and we caught a few strays with the ball. Just coming up behind Joe, his sixth sense kicked in."

Cole, who was in the middle, said: "The touch wasn't quite there, Woodsy. I had my head on the spin, I could tell something was coming." Woods quipped back: "I was expecting more from an ex-professional and now the sprinklers are coming for us.

"We're not having much luck so we'll move over here and get out the way. Hopefully someone has an umbrella for us."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Leeds were taking on the managerless London club as they looked to compound the misery on Chelsea, following Liam Rosenior's sacking in the wake of their 3-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion.

The drubbing was a seventh defeat out of eight for Chelsea after the Blues suffered a significant downturn of form under the former Hull City manager.

‌



Calum McFarlane was installed as caretaker for the second time this season after Enzo Maresca's unceremonious departure earlier in the season. The interim manager has been tasked with reigniting the spark at Stamford Bridge as they find themselves outside the European places.

View 2 Images Calum McFarlane is into his second spell in interim charge of Chelsea following Liam Rosenior's sacking. (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

The temporary boss claimed that the FA Cup semi-final under the arch at Wembley could motivate the Chelsea players after a poor run of form.

‌



He said: "Really disappointing. It was hard to watch that, hard to see that.

"To be dominated from minute one to minute 90. Brighton were very good but we were nowhere near our levels.

"Everything has been done that we possibly can to make sure the lads are as best prepared as they can be for what Leeds are going to throw at us and what we have to stand up to. I believe the players will be motivated to get to an FA Cup final."

Sports.title: What Ryan Reynolds' Wrexham need to reach Premier League as Championship play-off race goes to wire
Sports.content:
What Ryan Reynolds' Wrexham need to reach Premier League as Championship play-off race goes to wire

Phil Parkinson could guide Wrexham to the Premier League via the play-offs as 2025/26 comes to a close, but work still needs to be done

View 3 Images It looks to be an edgy week for Phil Parkinson (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Wrexham stand just 90 minutes away from securing a Championship play-off spot, with their destiny still narrowly within their own grasp. However, the room for mistakes couldn't be any slimmer following a 3-1 loss to champions Coventry City.

‌



Phil Parkinson's men appeared set to claim a vital point against Coventry on Sunday, which would have represented another significant stride towards the play-offs. Ollie Rathbone had equalised Brandon Thomas-Asante's opening goal to put them within touching distance of a draw, only for Victor Torp's late free-kick to dash Wrexham's hopes.

‌



Opportunities arose for Wrexham to rescue a point in the closing stages, but Kieffer Moore couldn't keep a header on target during stoppage time. That miss proved damaging as Ephron Mason-Clarke's strike in the 94th minute sealed victory for Coventry while also denting Wrexham's goal difference.

‌



Frank Lampard has revealed what he really thinks about Ryan Reynolds and Wrexham READ MORE :

Frank Lampard gives firm response to Chelsea job as Coventry boss addresses rumours READ MORE :

Having achieved remarkable back-to-back promotions from the National League through to the Championship since Hollywood actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney purchased the club, their aspirations of reaching the Premier League - and completing four promotions in four seasons - remain intact with just one fixture remaining.

Nevertheless, defeat to the Sky Blues has undoubtedly created tension ahead of next Saturday's finale...

What do Wrexham need to reach the play-offs?

Wrexham had entered their second-to-last league fixture of the campaign already occupying a play-off position, following Hull City's 2-1 loss to Charlton Athletic at The Valley. As well as securing their own Championship survival, the Addicks had done Wrexham a favour by keeping Hull out of the play-off spots.

‌



Wrexham had the chance to give themselves some breathing space following Hull's result, only for Coventry's two late strikes to shatter those hopes. Hull currently sit on 70 points, with a goal difference of +3.

Narrowly ahead of them are Wrexham. They also have 70 points, boasting a goal difference of +4. With that in mind, the margins for error heading into next week could not be any tighter.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



View 3 Images Wrexham suffered a heart-breaking loss to Coventry on Sunday (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Wrexham face promotion-chasing Middlesbrough next Saturday (May 2) at the STōK Cae Ras, while Hull host Norwich City. Derby County cannot be written off either, sitting eighth on 69 points and due to host Sheffield United next weekend.

The Rams' goal difference is superior to both Wrexham and Hull - currently standing at +9. All final day fixtures kick off at 12.30pm.

‌



Put simply, Wrexham just need to match or better the results of both Hull and Derby next weekend. Should Wrexham and Hull finish level on points, Wrexham's goal difference is currently in their favour - but only just.

The next tiebreaker, goals scored, edges in Hull's favour - having netted 68 times compared to Wrexham's 67. The final decider, head-to-head record, also favours Hull - having beaten Wrexham twice in the league this season.

Who could Wrexham face in the play-offs?

The question of who Wrexham could meet in the play-offs will be resolved next weekend — with several clubs still very much in contention. Coventry have already secured promotion as champions, having sealed a return to the Premier League following a 25-year absence.

‌



Beneath them, a group of clubs are battling it out for the final automatic promotion place. With two matches remaining, Ipswich Town are arguably best-positioned to make an immediate return to the top flight under Kieran McKenna.

The Tractor Boys climbed back into second spot on Saturday following a goalless stalemate with West Brom, sitting on 80 points with two fixtures left and a superior goal difference to their rivals. Victory against Southampton on Tuesday night would virtually guarantee promotion going into the final day of the campaign.

View 3 Images Rob McElhenney and Ryan Reynolds own Wrexham (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

‌



However, were the FA Cup semi-finalists - who suffered their first defeat since January after being beaten by Manchester City at Wembley - to triumph, then the four-way battle for second place would remain alive. Below Ipswich, Millwall currently sit on 80 points but with just one match remaining and a goal difference significantly worse than their competitors.

Wrexham's opponents next week, Middlesbrough, occupy fourth spot on 79 points. Southampton are presently fifth on 76 points, though they do have two matches still to play.

Should they reach the play-offs, Wrexham will need to focus on whichever club finishes third from those four sides. Their first leg would take place on Friday, May 8, at the STōK Cae Ras at 8pm.

Article continues below

The return leg would then be on Monday, May 11 at 8pm. The Championship play-off final is scheduled for Saturday, 23 May.

Sports.title: Mo Salah's injury 'worse than he thinks' as Steven Gerrard offers worrying update
Sports.content:
Mo Salah's injury 'worse than he thinks' as Steven Gerrard offers worrying update

Mohamed Salah could potentially have seen his Liverpool career ended prematurely with the Egyptian forward taken off the pitch midway through Saturday’s victory against Crystal Palace

View 2 Images Salah was injured in Liverpool's clash with Crystal Palace (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has warned that Mohamed Salah’s injury could potentially be worse than first feared. The Egyptian was taken off with a knock midway through the Reds’ 3-1 win against Crystal Palace.

‌



Reports have suggested that Salah has picked up a hamstring injury and could be ruled out for the next four weeks. That would mean that the 33-year-old’s Liverpool career is now over.

‌



Liverpool icon Gerrard has now spoken out and believes his injury could be even more severe but hopes that it will not completely rule him out for the remainder of the campaign.

‌



Speaking on TNT Sports, the former midfielder said: "It would be sad, but let's hope that's not the case [that he's played his final game]. It's worse than Mo probably thinks it is now, but until you can get it properly assessed by the medical team, and you have an MRI scan, you don't really know the extent.

Jamie Carragher identifies major problem with Alexander Isak that no one has talked about READ MORE :

Liverpool fan throws ball at Daniel Munoz's head after controversial Crystal Palace goal READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"But if it is the case that he's played his last game, that would be extremely sad - not just for Mo but for everyone connected with Liverpool Football Club, because he's been a legend and everyone wants to see him get the send-off he deserves."

‌



Liverpool boss Arne Slot gave an update on Salah immediately after the win against Palace. He said: ”We don’t know... that is the best answer I can give. If I say there might be a chance, that is probably the headline.

”We simply don’t know, but what we do know is that the season is over in four weeks. There are not a lot of games to be played, so we have to wait and see how his injury is and if he is able to return to play.

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard has offered his thoughts on Mo Salah's injury (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"What I do know about Mo is that for all these years he has taken so good care of his body that he will have the minimum time required to recover from an injury. Let’s hope for the best that he’s available. But another injury after a win, that sums up our season."

Liverpool will continue their push for a Champions League spot next weekend with or without Salah. The Reds take on Manchester United at Old Trafford at Old Trafford, with games against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Brentford to come.

Liverpool currently sit fourth in the Premier League table and level on points with both United and Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher identifies major problem with Alexander Isak that no one has talked about
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher identifies major problem with Alexander Isak that no one has talked about

Jamie Carragher has voiced concern over Alexander Isak's future at Liverpool and whether the Premier League's record signing will ever meet expectations

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has raised an alarming concern about Alexander Isak and his Liverpool future (Image: Sky Sports Premier League)

Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher has questioned whether Alexander Isak will justify his price tag at Anfield. The Premier League's all-time record signing has suffered a nightmarish debut season on Merseyside following his £125million switch from Newcastle last summer.

‌



Isak, 26, netted his fourth goal for the club in Saturday's 3-1 victory at home to Crystal Palace. His appearance against the Eagles represented his third start since returning from the leg fracture he sustained against Tottenham in December.

‌



Nevertheless, a considerable journey lies ahead before the Swede can be deemed to have warranted his staggering fee. And Carragher is deeply concerned given, in his experience, no player truly flourished at Liverpool after a poor maiden campaign.

‌



"[The big-spending summer] hasn't worked," he told the Liverpool Echo. "It might work in the future because I don't think you can judge every signing in the first year.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"But I've said this before; my experience as a Liverpool player, every player who came to the club, I can't remember one who didn't really do much in his first season, and then was a revelation afterwards. Isak hasn't got going. He obviously got the injury, but he didn't look great to start with."

‌



Liverpool manager Arne Slot gives worrying Mo Salah injury update after substitution READ MORE :

Liverpool sent clear Michael Olise transfer message by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

Isak's situation is rather unique in that several factors need to be taken into account. Arne Slot's squad were navigating a period of transition following their Premier League triumph last season and integrating £446million worth of fresh talent has presented its own set of complications.

The striker's leg injury towards the end of 2026 also dealt a further blow to his prospects, essentially rendering this campaign a lost cause as the side struggled even more without him. With that in mind, Champions League-winner Carragher offered his thoughts on what he believes must happen this summer to mount a renewed title challenge.

View 2 Images Isak's first season at Anfield has been hugely underwhelming (Image: Michael Regan - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images)

‌



"In terms of what Liverpool need to do next season, well obviously they need to replace [Mohamed] Salah," he added. "I think for me, three players need to come straight into the team."

"You can't go on and buy five players into the team. Liverpool bought a lot of players last summer, so they are not going to buy a load this summer."

The declining form of Salah and, on occasion, Virgil van Dijk, combined with Alisson's fitness problems, have held Liverpool back at times. Those three figures alone have been so vital to the Reds' recent period of success that it stands to reason the team should struggle when they're either out of sorts or unavailable.

Yet it's hard to fault supporters for feeling that excuse only stretches so far given a £446m summer splurge. And while Isak may be afforded some leeway for his disappointing debut campaign, Liverpool run the risk of overseeing the most embarrassing flop signing in Premier League history unless there's a dramatic turnaround next season.

Sports.title: Man Utd identify another Casemiro replacement as summer transfer plans step up
Sports.content:
Man Utd identify another Casemiro replacement as summer transfer plans step up

Manchester United have a significant gap to fill in their side this summer with Casemiro set to depart but the Red Devils already have a significant list of potential signings

View 2 Images Casemiro is due to leave Man United at the end of the season (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United have added Atalanta star Ederson to their shortlist as they attempt to sign a replacement for Casemiro. The former Real Madrid midfielder is due to leave at Old Trafford at the end of the season when his contract expires.

‌



That is set to come after arguably Casemiro’s most impressive season as a United player so far. And given the task that United chiefs have in replacing him, they have compiled an extensive list of candidates.

‌



Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, Nottingham Forest star Elliot Anderson, Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton and Real Madrid destroyer Aurelien Tchouameni are all among those United are eyeing. But Ederson has now emerged as another potential target, with the Brazilian looking likely to leave Atalanta.

‌



Ederson, 26, is out of contract next summer and is valued at €40m-50m (£35m-£45m). According to The Guardian, Jason Wilcox is an admirer of the midfielder and could pursue a move in the summer window.

13 Man Utd players who could be moved on in savage summer clear-out READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United however could face competition for his services, with Atletico Madrid also thought to be strongly interested. Speaking in February, the club’s sporting director Mateu Alemany said: “One more on the list of good players we have.”

‌



United reportedly want to sign two new midfielders this summer, albeit much could depend on the future of Manuel Ugarte. The Uruguayan has struggled for form since his arrival from Paris Saint-Germain.

Current United boss Michael Carrick has already underlined the importance of adding to United’s midfield ahead of next season, particularly given Casemiro’s exit.

View 2 Images Man United are interested in a move for Atalanta's Ederson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Speaking earlier this season, he said: "Yeah, well, listen, it's an important position. Not being biased, obviously, as being a midfielder, but I think it is an important position to try and tie everything together and you’re connected to the whole team, and that's sometimes emotionally, a little bit mentally, and showing that composure and understanding of the game a little bit.

"Case has had a big influence within the group on that. So, something we're fully aware of moving forward, for sure.”

Casemiro joined United in a big-money move from Real Madrid in 2022 and he has gone on to make 157 appearances, scoring 25 goals - eight of which have come this term. He could potentially make one of his final Old Trafford appearances on Monday evening when Carrick’s side host Brentford, while Liverpool and Nottingham Forest are set to come over the closing weeks of the campaign.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford makes clear Barcelona point amid Man Utd transfer scrutiny
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford makes clear Barcelona point amid Man Utd transfer scrutiny

Marcus Rashford showed his quality for Barcelona amid reports that a permanent move to Spain is teetering

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford's future following the end of his Barcelona loan remains uncertain (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United loanee Marcus Rashford got himself on the scoresheet for Barcelona in another week dominated by speculation surrounding his long-term future. The England international netted the second goal in their 2-0 victory over Getafe on Saturday as they took advantage of Real Madrid's stumble to move 11 points clear.

‌



Reports this week have indicated that Barcelona will not exercise Rashford's buyout clause, which would secure a permanent switch to Catalonia. It has emerged that Hansi Flick's side have performed a U-turn on their intention to trigger the option, reportedly worth around £26million, having struggled to negotiate a permanent deal with United.

‌



Speculation, namely from SPORT, suggests that sporting director Deco and Flick have reached an agreement that they are unwilling to pay the transfer fee or wages with the price described as 'too high'.

‌



On the pitch, Fermin Lopez broke the deadlock at the Estadio Coliseum on the stroke of half-time before Rashford wrapped up the three points 16 minutes from time. It was a quintessential Rashford goal as he used his electrifying pace to latch onto a ball played in behind the defence with Getafe having pushed men forward.

The forward drove towards goal and shrugged off two defenders before firing past the goalkeeper. Barcelona now boast a double-digit advantage at the top of Spanish football with just 15 points remaining.

13 Man Utd players who could be moved on in savage summer clear-out READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes issues Jamie Carragher apology after celebrating England failure READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



They have the opportunity to extinguish their title rivals' hopes of a late charge to derail the La Liga procession when Real Madrid make the trip to the Camp Nou on 10 May. Flick paid tribute to the United loanee as he put into perspective just how vital the Englishman's contribution, and 13th goal of the campaign, proved to be.

He said: "Marcus came on in the second half and he used the space they give us. We spoke about this at half time. I am happy for the team, for us and also for him that he scored this goal because it was so important for him and also for us.

View 3 Images Hansi Flick has praised the impact of the England star (Image: Xavi Bonilla/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

‌



"We [only] celebrate the victory. It's different. I said to the team before the game, we only focus on the day to day, on our job, what we have to do. When we play like this, I am really happy.

Sports.title: Gauff recovers from vomiting on court to beat Cirstea in feisty Madrid Open clash
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff recovered from feeling unwell and vomiting on court to beat Sorana Cirstea in feisty Mutua Madrid Open contest on Sunday.

The reigning French Open champion, runner-up here 12 months ago, overcame physical struggles, fighting back from a set and a break down to book her spot in the fourth round with a 4-6 7-5 6-1 win in the Spanish capital.

Gauff called for the physio in the second set and vomited on court after which she had her blood pressure check by the doctor.

"Because I'm there and they are bothering me because they are screaming in my ear."

"For me, I do not hear any coaching," the umpire replied.

Sports.title: Coventry celebrate title party with win as Wrexham sweat on play-offs
Sports.content:
Coventry celebrated their Sky Bet Championship title with a 3-1 victory that leaves Wrexham’s play-off ambitions in the balance.

The Sky Blues were in party mood after Frank Lampard's side had wrapped up the title on Tuesday and they lifted the trophy in front of their buoyant fans after the final whistle.

Brandon Thomas-Asante volleyed the hosts ahead after 19 minutes at the CBS Arena, but Ollie Rathbone replied quickly for sixth-placed Wrexham.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Coventry lift Championship trophy in celebration at the Coventry Building Society Arena!

A point would have been welcome for the visitors but - 10 minutes from time - substitute Victor Torp drove home a powerful free-kick which Danny Ward could only help into the roof of the net.

Ephron Mason-Clark put the cherry on Coventry's cake with a classy finish in the fourth minute of stoppage-time.

Addressing fans on the pitch as his players celebrated their silverware, Lampard said: "The biggest thing is the football club is only as big as the people who support it.

"You've been down a lot, you've been to different stadiums, because when you're born this way, you're never going to change. You've gone through everything.

"One of the biggest pleasures we get as a group is giving you the joy of this moment. This moment is yours."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Frank Lampard addressed the Coventry faithful after his side lifted the Championship trophy

Wrexham head into the last round of games on Saturday with the smallest of advantages in the race for the final play-off place.

Level on 70 points with Hull, they now have a superior goal difference of just one over the Tigers, while Derby remain in the hunt just a point back.

On what is sure to be a tense afternoon, all three finish at home, with Wrexham playing Middlesbrough, Hull hosting Norwich, while Derby entertain Sheffield United.

Thousands of Coventry fans held up "We Are Back" placards before kick-off to mark their return to the Premier League after a 25-year absence.

Wrexham were back at a stadium holding fond memories for their supporters following an FA Cup giant-killing in 2023 during the club's National League days.

The Sky Blues were given a guard of honour by opponents seeking a league double after their 3-2 Racecourse victory in October.

There were early shots blocked at either end with George Thomason and Frank Onyeka unable to find a way through congested defences.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brandon Thomas-Asante fires in the opener for Coventry in their clash with Wrexham.

The party atmosphere went up several notches when Thomas-Asante made a darting run between Callum Doyle and Thomason to fire home Mason-Clark's cross from a few yards out.

Coventry's lead remained intact for only six minutes as George Dobson delivered a delightful ball down the right for Issa Kabore.

The wing-back had space to attack and Rathbone dispatched his low cross from 14 yards out in emphatic fashion.

Although Coventry had two-thirds possession in the first half, Wrexham carried a threat on the counter-attack with Josh Windass rippling the side netting and Thomason striking an upright.

Ward made his first meaningful save 10 minutes after the restart to keep out out a Haji Wright header at the base of a post after the Sky Blues' top scorer was found by Milan van Ewijk.

Carl Rushworth was just as alert to prevent Sam Smith profiting from a Dobson's through ball that split the Coventry defence and the save was to prove crucial.

Torp won the argument to take the free-kick and the Danish midfielder produced a beauty before Mason-Clark crowned a season to remember for the Sky Blues.

The managers

Coventry's Frank Lampard:

"The first thing I must say is thanks to so many people. I want to thank this incredible group of players. We came together 16 months ago and we've added players along the way and everyone who has come in has added. This group is an amazing bunch of lads. Talented, together.

"Can I also thank every member of staff who works behind the scenes. They don't get the credit every week but they're as important.

"A massive thank you to Dean Austin who has recruited these brilliant players and then to Doug King.

"I can't miss out my wife and two children. Family is massive, all the wives, partners, children, parents who support them, thank you so much.

"The biggest thing is the football club is only as big as the people who support it. You've been down a lot, you've been to different stadiums, because when you're born this way, you're never going to change. You've gone through everything.

"One of the biggest pleasures we get as a group is giving you the joy of this moment. This moment is yours."

Sports.title: Wiesberger ends five-year wait for DP World Tour title
Sports.content:
Bernd Wiesberger ended his five-year wait for a DP World Tour title following victory at the China Open on Sunday.

The Austrian started the final round one shot adrift of overnight leader Adrian Otaegui but his round of 67 saw him finish 19-under and three strokes clear at the top of the leaderboard.

Otaegui (71) had a miserable back nine that saw him bogey twice and double-bogey the 18th at the Shanghai Enhance Anting Golf Club.

"It's been a tough couple of years," an emotional Wiesberger said. "An unbelievable week.

"I played my heart out today, it wasn't pretty at times but I got it done.

"Adrian is a great competitor and had it under control, but something happened on that tenth hole that I can't explain. That's how golf goes sometimes.

"I'm super proud of sticking through hard times on the golf course lately, but this is for everyone at home and couldn't be happier.

"Everyone is watching and super excited now, and it changes my next couple of years a little bit. It gets me into the Rolex Series events again and that's huge."

Sweden's Mikael Lindberg fired a final-round 67 to clinch solo third at 14 under, with South African early pacesetter Shaun Norris one shot further back in fourth.

German Freddy Schott carded the lowest round of Sunday with a 64 to take fifth at 12 under, France's Tom Vaillant and Englishman Nathan Kimsey shared sixth at 11-under and defending champion Ashun Wu led Alejandro Del Rey, Darius van Driel, Antoine Rozner and Anthony Quayle one shot further back.

Wiesberger's last victory came at the Danish Golf Championship in May 2021.

Sports.title: Hong Kong superstar Ka Ying Rising extends winning streak to 20
Sports.content:
Ka Ying Rising cemented his status as the world’s best sprinter by extending his winning run to 20 with victory in the Chairman’s Sprint Prize at Sha Tin.

Despite not being asked for everything by his regular partner Zac Purton, the local superstar again broke the track record at the Hong Kong circuit as he came home four and a quarter lengths clear of his toiling rivals. Multiple Japanese Group One winner and Royal Ascot runner-up Satono Reve best of the rest in second and Donnacha O'Brien's Irish raider Comanche Brave fifth of the eight runners.

The David Hayes-trained Ka Ying Rising was completing the Hong Kong Speed Series for a second year in a row after previously coming out on top in the Centenary Sprint Cup and Queen's Silver Jubilee Cup.

Hayes, who confirmed he will now give his charge a break before preparing him to defend his title in The Everest in Australia in October, said: "You tend to worry that you are going to let everyone down. He doesn't, does he? In the year of the horse, he is now one of the all-time greats, I think. The way he is running times and rating so incredibly well.

"A long time ago I thought he might have been the best horse I trained and about a year ago I thought he was definitely the best horse I trained. Now I think he is one of the best horses I have ever seen."

Another Hong Kong great Romantic Warrior timed his challenge to perfection to win the FWD QEII Cup for a fourth time.

Image: Romantic Warrior (1) ridden by James McDonald wins the Longines Hong Kong Cup (Group 1) at Sha Tin. Kaz Ishida/Eclipse Sportswire/CSM

Held in the pack by James McDonald, he started to make headway a furlong and a half out and quickly took control, winning eased down by a length.

Masquerade Ball, who has only beaten a head by Calandagan in the Japan Cup, stayed on well to take second, with Andre Fabre's Sosie one and quarter lengths further back in third ahead of Karl Burke's Royal Champion in fourth.

Harry Eustace's Docklands did not disgrace himself as he stayed on well to take third in the middle of the three Group Ones on the card, the FWD Champions Mile.

The race started to take shape a furlong out as My Wish came out of the pack to lay down the challenge, with Docklands following him through.

My Wish held on to edge out the fast-finishing Cap Ferrat, who headed Dockland close home to hold him off by half a length.

Docklands' jockey Mark Zahra said: "He ran super. He settled back nice and comfy off - not a hectic speed, but he got the split at the right time, and credit to him for running third."

Sports.title: Sawe smashes two-hour barrier to make history at London Marathon
Sports.content:
London Marathon 2026: Sabastian Sawe becomes first man to run marathon under two hours with stunning world record

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sabastian Sawe becomes the first person ever to run an official marathon in under two hours, after winning the London Marathon Sabastian Sawe becomes the first person ever to run an official marathon in under two hours, after winning the London Marathon

Sabastian Sawe of Kenya smashed the men's world record by winning the 2026 London Marathon in 1 hour, 59 minutes and 30 seconds on Sunday.

His incredible run wiped 35 seconds off the previous record held by the late Kelvin Kiptum, who ​set a time ​of ​2:00:35 at the 2023 Chicago Marathon.

Yomif Kejelcha of Ethiopia stayed on Sawe's heels over much of the ​42.195-kilometre course before fading down the final ⁠stretch to take second ⁠in his marathon debut with 1:59.41, while Jacob Kiplimo of Uganda took the ‌bronze in 2:02.28.

"For the new generation (it shows) to run a record is possible," Sawe, who made a solo break in the final two kilometres as he sprinted down The Mall past Buckingham Palace.

"Everything is possible with a matter of time. I was ready today. I was well-prepared for the London Marathon and for today's results. I'm so happy because I had a lot of courage to push, even when the pace was fast."

Kejelcha was full of praise for Sawe's mission to prove his races are clean, which included taking 25 extra voluntary drug tests before winning the Berlin Marathon.

Kejelcha added: "It's very important for clean sport. Maybe I, for the future, will do the same thing. I think it's a great idea."

Sawe's record run - average pace required 1k: 2:50

2:50 5k: 14:10

14:10 10k: 28:19

28:19 1 mile 4:33

4:33 Half marathon: 59:45

'The goalposts have moved for marathon running'

Breaking two hours in a marathon has been a long time coming.

Eliud Kipchoge, the Kenyan long-distance great, in fact achieved the feat in Vienna in 2019, but in a specially tailored race called the "1.59 Challenge" that was arranged by British billionaire and now Manchester United co-owner Jim Ratcliffe in favourable conditions on a six-mile circuit using rotating pacemakers.

That meant it was not classed as an official race setting, so Kipchoge's time of 1:59:40 did not go in the record book.

Sawe went on to surpass that time by 10 seconds on a mostly flat course across London in dry, sunny conditions.

"The goalposts have literally just moved for marathon running," former London marathon winner Paula Radcliffe said during commentary of the race for the BBC.

At the turn of the century, the world's best time for the men's marathon was 2:05:42, set by Khalid Khannouchi in Chicago in 1999.

Khannouchi broke his own record by four seconds in 2002 - the last time the fastest men's marathon was run in London - and it has been whittled down gradually over the last 24 years by a succession of Kenyan and Ethiopian runners including Haile Gebrselassie, Wilson Kipsang, Kipchoge and, most recently, Kiptum.

Assefa breaks own record to win women's title

Tigst Assefa celebrates after winning the women's elite race at the 2026 London Marathon

Tigst Assefa of Ethiopia retained the women's title with a time of 2:15:41 breaking her own record from last year's London Marathon.

The 29-year-old pulled away from Kenyans Hellen Obiri and Joyciline Jepkosgei down ⁠the home stretch to cross the ​finish line in 2:15.41 seconds, beating the ​record of 2:15.50 she set last year ​in London.

That, however, was 16 seconds slower than the course record set by Paula Radcliffe in 2003 when it was a mixed race.

Obiri was second in 2:15.53, while Jepkosgei ⁠took the bronze in 2:15.55.

Switzerland's Marcel Hug and Catherine Debrunner won the men's and women's wheelchair events.

Hug won for the sixth consecutive ​year and eighth overall, while Debrunner outsprinted ​American Tatyana McFadden to the finish for her third consecutive win in London.
